text:
Carter Verhaeghe has three Stanley Cups, one in Tampa and two in Florida, and he's playing like a man used to scoring in big games. He has nine goals and 15 points in 17 games, seven of them on the power play.

Here's the catch, and it's a big one. Nine goals on 6.4 expected (the quality of his chances) means he's shooting 26%, double last season's 13%, and Florida has scored 8.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of luck that rarely lasts a season. The process underneath is solid rather than spectacular: at 5v5 the Panthers get about 54% of the expected goals with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving his own zone with the puck 72% of the time last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best. Our projection has 25 to 40 more goals. He's still a good top-six winger. Just not quite this good.
headline: Verhaeghe is hot; the luck is hotter
